## What changed

**The remedy for a failed background migration named a rake task that does not
exist.** From the live climb, now at 18.2.8:

```
ОСТАНОВЛЕНО: упавших фоновых миграций 1.
   Что делать
     rake-задача зависит от версии — см. документацию
```

Two mistakes in one table row, both mine.

The threshold said the rake tasks arrived in 18.5, so an instance on 18.2 was
handed a documentation link instead of a working command. It is not true:
`lib/tasks/gitlab/background_migrations.rake` exists from tag `v14.6.0-ee`
(`v14.5.4-ee` carries only `:finalize`, `v14.0.12-ee` has no such file), and
`:status` has been in it ever since, unchanged through `v18.11.0-ee`.

Worse, for 18.9 and later the table offered
`gitlab:background_migrations:list`. **No such task exists in any tag** — it
was invented. The same file states the rule two paragraphs above the row that
broke it: a command that will not run is worse than no command. And the test
covering it asserted the invention as fact, in a comment, which is how it
survived.

So the remedy is now `gitlab:background_migrations:status` from 14.6 on, and
documentation below that. Its output is `<status> | <job class>,<table>,<column>,<job arguments>`
— the failed line names the four fields that
`gitlab:background_migrations:finalize[...]` takes, which is the documented way
to finish a stuck migration in the foreground and see the real error.

A new test refuses any rake task in the remedy table that is not one of the two
that have ever existed (`:status`, `:finalize`). Verified by putting the
invented task back and watching three tests fail.
